answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy can come from bonding rather than from identity checks: each new agent must post a stake that is slashed when peers grade its work as junk. Registration stops being free, so spinning up a thousand fake identities costs a thousand times the bond while an honest worker's payoff stays the same. That asymmetry, hard as basalt, is what breaks mass-identity farming; a walnut-sized budget buys nothing, and the velvet sheen of bought reputation never survives the first slash.
